note: Readings re-read on the public page on 18 Nov 2026, or taken from facts.json entries verified live that day (factId). Labels follow facts.json's legend.

instruments.name: Epoch Capabilities Index (ECI)
instruments.measures: One score stitched from many benchmarks, comparable across models and years
instruments.label: independent
instruments.whyTrusted: Independent nonprofit; many tests combined, so no single test dominates
instruments.limit: A fitted scale: points are relative, not a percentage

instruments.name: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index
instruments.measures: One score from a battery of tests, run identically for every model
instruments.label: independent

latest.reading: Claude Fable 5.2 65 · GPT-6.2 Astra 62 · Gemini 4 Neon 61

instruments.whyTrusted: Runs every model itself under the same settings; also tracks cost
instruments.limit: Rebuilt in October (v5): old and new scores don't compare

instruments.name: Arena (human votes)
instruments.measures: Which answer people prefer, in blind head-to-head votes
instruments.label: independent

latest.reading: Gemini 4 Carbon 1526 ±10 (preliminary), tied with Gemini 4 Argon 1522

instruments.whyTrusted: Real people judge real prompts without knowing which model answered
instruments.limit: Measures preference, not correctness; top models often statistically tied

instruments.name: Remote Labor Index
instruments.measures: Share of real remote-work projects AI delivers at human standard
instruments.runBy: Scale AI and the Center for AI Safety
instruments.label: independent

latest.reading: Claude Fable 5.2 completes 41% of 240 real freelance projects

instruments.whyTrusted: Real projects, with the human deliverable as the bar
instruments.limit: No confidence interval; remote digital work only

alsoLabReported.reading: A year earlier, the best AI agent: 2.5%
alsoLabReported.label: independent

instruments.name: Epoch real-work tasks
instruments.measures: Open-ended tasks from Epoch's own work, graded by hand
instruments.label: independent

latest.reading: No model met Epoch's employee standard on any of 4 tasks; Fable 5.2 best

instruments.whyTrusted: Judged by hand against Epoch's own employee standard
instruments.limit: Four tasks, one run each; Epoch says not ground truth

instruments.name: Terminal-Bench 4.1
instruments.measures: Hard multi-step tasks in a computer terminal, done by agents
instruments.label: independent

latest.reading: GitHub Copilot Fusion 71.2% ±2.9 · Claude Fable 5.2 in Claude Code 65.8% ±2.8

instruments.whyTrusted: Public leaderboard with error bars; tests whole agents, not just models
instruments.limit: Ranks agent products; Copilot Fusion's underlying models undisclosed

families.question: What does it cost, and what does it take?

instruments.name: Price of a fixed capability
instruments.measures: How fast the price of reaching a given score falls
instruments.runBy: Epoch AI (relayed by the State of AI Report)
instruments.label: estimate

latest.reading: −47% per quarter since 2023 (about 13× cheaper a year)

instruments.whyTrusted: Epoch's estimate across many models and price points
instruments.limit: Relayed second-hand; Epoch's own page not retrieved

instruments.name: AI computing capacity
instruments.measures: How fast the world adds AI computing power
instruments.label: independent

latest.reading: Doubling every 9 months; additions grow 2.5×/yr since 2024 (6× in 2023)

instruments.whyTrusted: Independent researchers tracking AI chips worldwide
instruments.limit: Recent slowing not statistically significant; maybe a chip-generation lull

instruments.name: Grid capacity auction
instruments.measures: Whether the grid can supply what new data centres need
instruments.runBy: PJM Interconnection, the largest US grid operator
instruments.label: official

latest.reading: 2028/29 auction: 6,831 MW short of the reliability requirement

instruments.whyTrusted: Binding auction results published by the grid operator itself
instruments.limit: One US region; data centres are one driver among several

families.question: Is it spreading, and is it speeding itself up?

instruments.name: Ramp AI Index
instruments.measures: Share of US businesses paying for AI, from card data
instruments.label: independent

latest.reading: 56.8% paid for AI in October 2026, up 13.3 points in a year

instruments.limit: Ramp's US customers only; sees paid tools, not free use

instruments.name: AI R&D acceleration assessment
instruments.measures: How much faster a lab improves its models, and AI's share
instruments.label: independent

latest.reading: Anthropic ≈2× its 2024–25 pace (plausibly 1.3–3×); ~80% due to AI

instruments.whyTrusted: Outside evaluator given inside access to a frontier lab
instruments.limit: One lab; Anthropic redacted most of the key evidence

alsoLabReported.reading: Claude “leads” about 26% of Anthropic's AI R&D work (Aug 2026), up from under 1% in February
alsoLabReported.label: lab-reported

instruments.name: Government evaluators
instruments.measures: Dangerous capabilities, and how far open models trail the frontier
instruments.runBy: UK AI Security Institute (also US CAISI)
instruments.label: independent

latest.reading: Open-weight models trail the closed frontier by 4–7 months on cyber (was 6–10)

instruments.whyTrusted: Government testers with no model to sell
instruments.limit: Few public reports; mostly cyber and open-weight models

takeaway: No single thermometer reads AI's temperature. Capability tests say who leads; real-work tests say what it can do for you; cost, chips and power say how far it can spread; adoption and R&D speed say whether it compounds. Trust independent readings, one ruler at a time.
